title: Put Marbles in Bags
summary: Given k bags and an array of marble weights, distribute the marbles such that no bag is empty, and if marbles i and j are in a bag, all marbles between i and j must also be in the same bag.
statement: Given k bags and an array of marble weights, distribute the marbles such that no bag is empty, and if marbles i and j are in a bag, all marbles between i and j must also be in the same bag. Calculate the cost for each bag as the sum of the first and last marble's weights in the bag. The score is the total cost of all bags. Return the difference between the highest and lowest possible scores from different distributions.
constraints: Split the ordered marbles into exactly k nonempty contiguous bags.
Each bag contributes its first weight plus its last weight.
Return maximum possible total score minus minimum possible total score.
hints: The outermost first and last weights occur in every partition and cancel in the difference.
A cut between adjacent marbles adds the sum of those two boundary weights.
Choose the k-1 largest boundary sums for the maximum score and the k-1 smallest for the minimum.
All cut choices contribute independently once the fixed outer endpoints cancel, so sorting boundary sums is sufficient.
editorial: All cut choices contribute independently once the fixed outer endpoints cancel, so sorting boundary sums is sufficient.

tests.explanation: Choosing the largest versus smallest single cut-boundary pair changes the score by four.
Both marbles must be separate, so maximum and minimum scores are identical.
